Modern PG: autovacuum runs automatically — tune via `autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor` etc.

entries.title: psql recipe: use transactions safely
entries.statement: Explicit: `BEGIN; UPDATE ...; SELECT ...; COMMIT;` or `ROLLBACK;`. Inside psql: `\set ON_ERROR_ROLLBACK on` continues transaction on error (vs the default of aborting on first error). Savepoints: `SAVEPOINT s1; ... ROLLBACK TO s1; ... COMMIT;`. Isolation: `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;` (strictest) or `REPEATABLE READ`. Default isolation: READ COMMITTED.

entries.title: psql recipe: create an index concurrently (no lock)
entries.statement: Standard: `CREATE INDEX ON users (email);` — locks table briefly. Production-safe: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON users (email);` — no exclusive lock, takes longer. Always CONCURRENTLY on production tables.

entries.statement: Skip duplicate: `INSERT INTO users (id, email) VALUES (1, 'a@x') ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;`. entries.title: psql recipe: configure connection pooling with PgBouncer
entries.statement:
Not PostgreSQL itself — but the standard solution. Install pgbouncer + config /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini: ```
[databases]
mydb = host=localhost port=5432 dbname=mydb

[pgbouncer]
listen_port = 6432
pool_mode = transaction
max_client_conn = 1000
default_pool_size = 25
```. Connect via pgbouncer: `psql -h pgbouncer-host -p 6432 -d mydb`. Modes: `session` (per-client), `transaction` (per-transaction, most common), `statement` (most aggressive).
